subAgents: none: dispatch forbids spawning. All work and all verification done by this agent.
missionPremise: The chrome does not follow the pack. Carried forward by _inbox/2026-08-18_g76_g79_fixture_city_and_type.md: on empty-city the top bar reads 'City of Template TX', the seal reads CT, the nav footer reads '1 of 12 sources connected | template-city', and only the breadcrumb is correct. web/app.js has zero references to brandcity. _decisions/2026-08-18_template_city_becomes_fixture_city.md makes a pack switch the demo mechanism, so a half switch defeats the ruling.
completionPredicate: On /?cityKey=empty-city no rendered string names Template, and on /?cityKey=template-city every identity surface names Template city; both resolve for an anonymous caller with DASHBOARDS_API_KEY set; every figure in the chrome is true for the pack being viewed and carries its counting rule at the point of use; web/shell.css and web/sc-kit.css are blob-identical to origin/main.
scopeBasis: The card names six surfaces but governs 'identity resolves from the active pack, everywhere it appears', and the constraint 'static markup must not name a city that the active pack is not' reaches every one of the 16 'City of Template' / 'template-city' literals in web/index.html, not just the six. Out of scope by ruling: src/municode-calendar.mjs and src/adapters.mjs internal Bastrop refusal strings (server-side guards, never rendered); the accessPolicy of the existing /api/city-packs enumeration gate (must stay shut, unchanged); 404-vs-401 existence disclosure on tenant-private keys (pre-existing in packReadStatus, unchanged, named not fixed); web/shell.css and web/sc-kit.css (G-81 owns shell.css).

designDecisions.decision: New module src/city-identity.mjs is the single resolver. It derives seal initials, state suffix, environment badge and the per-pack source figure from a pack object and nothing else.
designDecisions.why: Chrome identity had no owner, which is why it was static markup. One module means one place a test can measure against.
designDecisions.rejected: Reusing /api/lenses/development-services/pipeline for chrome identity. It couples the top bar to one lens's fixture generation, is irrelevant on Finance and Citizen, and carries no seal, state or grants.

designDecisions.decision: New endpoint GET /api/city-identity?cityKey= gated by packContentReadStatus, not packReadStatus.
designDecisions.why: Public-free pack identity is content per the G-78 fix. Enumeration via /api/city-packs stays on canReadPack and stays shut when DASHBOARDS_API_KEY is set. Tenant-private still refuses anonymous.
designDecisions.leakCheck: Returns cityKey, displayName, environment, accessPolicy, generatesFixtures, seal, state and a grant COUNT. Does not return notes or the grant list. No new existence-disclosure class beyond the pre-existing /api/city-packs/:key behaviour.

designDecisions.decision: Declarative binding in web/app.js: [data-pack-name] takes displayName, [data-pack-key] takes cityKey. Static content of every such element is fallback vocabulary ('This city', 'this pack'), never a city.
designDecisions.why: 16 literals across 12 breadcrumbs, 4 absence bases and the citizen copy. A per-element id would be 16 remembered edits; an attribute contract is one mechanism plus a structural test that counts crumbs against hooks.

designDecisions.decision: The city name inside .brandcity is a <data> element, not <span> or <b>.
designDecisions.why: .brandcity span is a real rule (font-weight 400, ink-3) so a span would render the city name as the quiet state suffix; <b> computes bolder against font-weight 600, which lands on 900. <data> carries no UA style and needs no class. No CSS file is edited and no class is added.

designDecisions.decision: renderPipeline stops writing ds-crumb-city. applyIdentity becomes the only writer of every identity surface.
designDecisions.why: DEV_PROCESS 2.4. Two writers for one fact is the CTRL-1 shape. A divergence test asserts composePipeline(pack).displayName equals cityIdentity(pack).displayName for all three packs, so the two paths cannot drift silently.

designDecisions.decision: Nav footer figure ruling: distinct adapter kinds granted on the pack being viewed, of the adapter catalog. Today 0 of 7 on every pack. The register's product figure 1 of 12 stays on the Connections page and gains its own inline counting rule.
designDecisions.why: The register counts feed-integration build dispositions product-wide; its 1 counts ArcGIS/Esri as Mounted through the SmartSite embed, which is granted on no pack. Beside a city name that number is false for the city. Numerator counts DISTINCT kinds so it can never exceed the denominator when a pack carries two grants of one kind. Verb differs deliberately: 'sources granted' in the footer, 'sources connected' on Connections, so two adjacent ratios cannot be read as the same class.
designDecisions.countingRuleTravelsWith: rendered inline in the footer beside the number, not in a tooltip and not in an appendix

designDecisions.decision: scripts/bake-connections.mjs stops baking nav-sources and keeps baking connections-sources.
designDecisions.why: The bake script writes web/index.html. Left alone it would rewrite the per-pack footer back to the register figure on its next run. DEV_PROCESS 6.3: correct state resting on something that a rerun reverts is a defect. scripts/ was not named in the card's ownership line; this is a declared extension, one file, tightly coupled to a file the card does own.
designDecisions.conflictRisk: none with G-81, which owns web/shell.css

designDecisions.decision: Static environment badge stays the literal Demo.
designDecisions.why: It names no city, all three shipped packs are environment demo, and the fail direction is safe: over-labelling a live city as Demo understates, under-labelling a fixture as Live is the labelling-gate failure the ruling exists to prevent. The G-77 divergence test that measures the shipped badge against environmentBadgeLabel(TEMPLATE_CITY) is kept, and a runtime test is added for live and staging.

adversarialReview: Q: does the new endpoint widen the anonymous surface? A: it exposes strictly less than /api/city-packs/:key already does for a readable pack, and it is gated on content policy rather than deployment posture, which is the G-78 correction applied forward rather than a new hole.

Q: could the footer ratio mislead once a real city is onboarded? A: numerator is distinct granted kinds intersected with the catalog, so an unknown kind cannot inflate it; the raw grant count travels in the payload beside it so the two numbers are reconcilable rather than silently merged.

Q: what breaks if the identity fetch fails? A: chrome holds the fallback vocabulary and names no city. That is strictly better than today, where a failed read leaves the wrong city asserted. Named as an untested-in-production path in the close.

Q: does removing the pipeline's crumb write lose anything? A: on a pack whose identity read fails but whose pipeline read succeeds the crumb stays at fallback. Accepted: one writer beats a fallback that fills in from a second source.
Q: is the character-set rule at risk? A: no dashes are introduced into any parsed source; the state separator is the existing middle dot.
